topics.title: What do we measure, and with what?

learn.hook: How tall is the tree? How heavy is the watermelon? How hot is the tea? Each question measures something different!
points: We measure many things: length (how long), height (how tall), breadth (how wide), depth (how deep), weight (how heavy) and temperature (how hot or cold).
Length, height, breadth and depth are all measured in units of length, like cm and m.
A ruler or scale (15 cm or 30 cm) measures small things like a pencil.
A metre stick measures 1 m at a time, good for a table or a door.
A measuring tape rolls up and can measure long or curved things, like a room or your waist.

example.q: Which tool is best to measure the length of the classroom?
steps: A classroom is many metres long.
A 30 cm scale would need too many moves.
A long measuring tape is best.

learn.reallife: Tailors use a soft measuring tape, carpenters use a metal tape, and you use a scale in your geometry box!

quiz.q: 'How deep is the well?' asks about which measurement?
quiz.explain: How deep means depth, the distance down.
steps: 'How deep' asks how far down something goes.
Height is how tall, so the answer is Depth.

quiz.q: Which tool is best to measure the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so a small scale works best.
steps: A pencil is short, only a few centimetres long.
A 15 cm scale is small and measures length.
A 30 m tape is too long; a weighing scale and thermometer don't measure length.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tool that does not measure length

quiz.q: A tailor measures the round waist of a customer. Which tool does she use?
quiz.explain: A soft tape can bend around curved things.
steps: A waist is round and curved.
A soft measuring tape can bend around curved things.
A stiff scale or metre stick cannot, so she uses a soft tape.
quiz.mistake: Picks a stiff tool for a curved shape

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a measure of length?
quiz.explain: Temperature tells how hot or cold, not how long.
steps: Depth, height and breadth are all lengths: how deep, how tall, how wide.
Temperature tells how hot or cold something is.
So temperature is NOT a measure of length.

quiz.q: 'How wide is the window?' Which word is used for how wide something is?
steps: How wide something is, is its breadth.
Height is how tall; depth is how deep.

quiz.q: A metre stick is how long?
quiz.explain: A metre stick is 1 m, which is 100 cm.
steps: A metre stick is 1 m long.
So a metre stick is 100 cm long.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metre and 30 cm scale

quiz.q: Ramu wants to know how hot his milk is. What does he measure?
steps: How hot or cold something is, is its temperature.
Weight, depth and length do not tell hotness.

quiz.q: Which is the best tool to measure the length of the school corridor?
quiz.explain: A long corridor needs a long measuring tape.
steps: A school corridor is many metres long.
A 10 cm thread, 30 cm ruler or 15 cm scale is too short.
A long measuring tape is best.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to measure his classroom with his little 15 cm scale. Suggest what to measure with which tool.
teach.praise: Scale for small things, tape for long things! The classroom needs a tape.
teach.nudge: Which tool suits long things and which suits small things?

revise.summary: We measure length, height, breadth, depth, weight and temperature. Length, height, breadth and depth use units like cm and m, measured with a scale, a metre stick or a measuring tape.
focus: Match words like how deep, how wide and how tall to the right measurement
Choose the best tool to measure a length
Tell which measurements are not lengths
remember: Depth: how deep. Breadth: how wide. Height: how tall
Scale (15 cm or 30 cm) for small things; metre stick for 1 m at a time; measuring tape for long or curved things
A metre stick is 1 m = 100 cm
traps: Don't mix up depth and height, or breadth and height
Temperature and weight are not lengths
Don't use a stiff tool for a curved shape like a waist

topics.title: Feeling a metre: jumps and the classroom

learn.hook: Walk 1 metre, jump 5 metres, crawl 10 metres! How do they feel?
points: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up. 5 m is about 5 big steps. 10 m is twice 5 m.
In a long jump contest, measure each jump with a rope or tape and write it in a table.
The longest jump has the biggest number; the shortest has the smallest.
Estimate first (a smart guess), then measure the length and breadth of the classroom to check.

example.q: Long jumps: Asha 2 m 10 cm, Babu 1 m 85 cm, Chetan 2 m 25 cm. Who jumped the longest?

learn.reallife: On sports day, long jump results are written on a board in metres and centimetres to pick the winner.

items.q: 10 m is how many 1 m lengths?
Classroom 8 m long, 6 m wide: length − breadth

quiz.q: Long jumps: Ravi 210 cm, Sita 185 cm, Tara 225 cm. Who jumped the shortest?
quiz.explain: 185 is the smallest, so Sita's jump was shortest.
steps: The jumps are 210 cm, 185 cm and 225 cm.
The shortest jump is the smallest number: 185.

quiz.q: In the same contest, how much longer was Tara's jump than Sita's?
steps: Tara jumped 225 cm; Sita jumped 185 cm.

quiz.q: Naren marks 10 m on the ground. How many 1 m lengths is that?
quiz.explain: 10 m is ten lengths of 1 m.
steps: 10 m means ten lengths of 1 m each.
So it is 10 lengths of 1 m.

quiz.q: Jaya guessed her classroom is 10 m long. She measured 8 m. How far off was her guess?
A classroom is 9 m long and 7 m wide. How much longer is its length than its breadth?
A child crawls 5 m, then walks another 5 m. How far did the child go?
steps: The child goes 5 m and then 5 m more.

quiz.q: Why do we write each jump in a table?
options: To compare jumps and find the longest and shortest
quiz.explain: A table keeps all the measurements in one place so we can compare them.
steps: A table puts all the jumps in one place.
Then we can easily compare them.
So we can find the longest and shortest jumps.
Answer: To compare jumps and find the longest and shortest
quiz.mistake: Does not see the use of a table

quiz.q: Jumps: Mohan 1 m 95 cm, Leena 2 m. Who jumped longer and by how much?
quiz.explain: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 − 195 = 5 cm. Leena jumped longer.

teach.ask: Gappu jumped 1 m 80 cm and Bubbly jumped 2 m 5 cm. Gappu thinks 80 is bigger, so he won. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: 180 cm and 205 cm! Bubbly jumped further. I must change everything to cm first.
teach.nudge: What happens if you change both jumps to centimetres?

revise.summary: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up. In a long jump contest, measure each jump, write it in a table and compare: the longest jump has the biggest number.
focus: Find the longest and shortest jump from a table
Find how much longer one length is than another
Estimate first, then measure to check
remember: 1 m is about one big step of a grown-up
2 m = 200 cm, so 2 m is 5 cm more than 1 m 95 cm
traps: Don't pick the longest when the shortest is asked
Don't add when 'how much longer' or 'how far off' is asked
Don't compare m and cm without first changing m to cm

topics.title: Guess the length from what you know

learn.hook: A bus is 10 m long. A crocodile is half as long as the bus. How long is the crocodile?
points: If you know the length of one thing, you can work out others from it.
Half as long means divide by 2. Twice as long means multiply by 2.
When things are stacked one on top of another, add their heights.
Compare a stacked height with another length by adding first, then comparing.

example.q: A cricket bat is about 1 m long. A whale is about 25 bats long. About how long is the whale?

learn.reallife: Wildlife books often say things like 'an ostrich is taller than a man' or 'a blue whale is as long as 3 buses'.

games.title: Taller or longer?
items: A 70 cm table with a 40 cm box on it is taller than 1 m.
Half of a 12 m bus is 24 m.
Two 50 cm stools stacked are as tall as 1 m.
An ostrich 2 m tall is taller than a 150 cm child.
Three 30 cm books stacked are 1 m tall.

quiz.q: A bus is 12 m long. A crocodile is half as long. How long is the crocodile?
steps: Half as long means divide by 2.

quiz.q: An ostrich is 2 m tall. A giraffe is 3 times as tall. How tall is the giraffe?
steps: 3 times as tall means multiply by 3.

quiz.q: A cricket bat is 1 m. A whale is as long as 20 bats. How long is the whale?
steps: Each bat is 1 m; the whale is 20 bats long.

quiz.q: A stool is 45 cm tall. A box of 35 cm is put on it. How tall is the stack?
steps: The box sits on top of the stool, so add the heights.

quiz.q: A table is 75 cm tall. A pot of 30 cm is kept on it. Is the top of the pot higher than a 1 m stick standing next to it?
A snake is 3 m long. A lizard is 30 cm long. How many lizards laid end to end are as long as the snake?
quiz.mistake: Does not change m to cm

quiz.q: Three bricks, each 10 cm high, are stacked. How tall is the stack?
steps: 3 bricks, each 10 cm high, stacked → add or multiply.

quiz.q: A train coach is 20 m long. A car is 4 m long. How many cars fit along one coach?

teach.ask: Gappu knows a bus is 10 m long. Gappu wants to know how long a crocodile half the bus's length is. Explain.
teach.praise: Half of 10 m is 5 m! I can find lengths using things I already know.
teach.nudge: What does 'half as long' tell you to do?

revise.summary: If you know the length of one thing, you can work out others from it. Half as long means divide by 2, twice as long means multiply by 2, and stacked heights are added.
focus: Use half as long, twice as long and times as long
Add the heights of stacked things and compare
Find how many of one thing make another, after changing units
remember: Half as long: ÷ 2. Twice as long: × 2
Stacked one on another: add their heights
3 m = 300 cm, so 300 ÷ 30 = 10 lizards
traps: Don't double when the question says half
Don't add 3 when it says 3 times as tall
Don't divide m by cm; change m to cm first

learn.hook: Diwali lights, garlands and ribbons: how much do we need altogether? Let's add lengths!
points: To add or subtract lengths, first make the units the same.
If you get 100 cm or more, change 100 cm into 1 m: 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm.
To find how much longer, subtract the shorter length from the longer one.
To find how much is left after cutting, subtract the cut part.

example.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length in m and cm?

learn.reallife: When you decorate for Diwali, you add up the lengths of light strings to see if they will cover the balcony.

quiz.q: Meena's plait is 45 cm long. How much shorter is it than 1 m?
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake taking away from 100, or adds instead

quiz.q: Riya has a 3 m rope. She cuts off 120 cm for a swing. How much rope is left?
quiz.mistake: Takes 3 away from 120 without changing metres to cm

quiz.q: Kabir runs 5 rounds of a 100 m track. How far does he run?
steps: One round = 100 m. Kabir runs 5 rounds.

quiz.q: Arjun is 1 m 32 cm tall. His sister is 1 m 18 cm tall. How much taller is Arjun?
steps: 1 m 32 cm = 132 cm, 1 m 18 cm = 118 cm
quiz.mistake: Adds the heights or takes away wrongly

quiz.q: Aisha joins 4 garland pieces, each 60 cm long. What is the total length?
quiz.mistake: Writes 240 cm as 240 m, or adds 4 + 60

quiz.q: Joseph's desk is 1 m long. How many 25 cm long books fit end to end along it?
quiz.mistake: Takes away 25 from 100 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Harpreet walks 650 m to school and then 650 m back home. How far does she walk in all?
steps: To school = 650 m; back home = 650 m.

quiz.q: Meena has a 75 cm ribbon and a 50 cm ribbon. What is their total length?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 2 m string and a 50 cm string. Gappu says together they are 52. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thank you! Change 2 m to 200 cm first, then add: 250 cm, which is 2 m 50 cm!
teach.nudge: Are metres and centimetres the same unit? What should Gappu do first?

revise.summary: To add or subtract lengths, first make the units the same. If you get 100 cm or more, change 100 cm into 1 m.
focus: Add lengths and write the answer in m and cm
Find how much longer or shorter
Find what is left after cutting
remember: 125 cm = 1 m 25 cm
How much longer: subtract the shorter from the longer
traps: Don't take away without changing m to cm first
Don't write 125 cm as 125 m
Don't count only one way for a there-and-back walk

learn.hook: Is your classroom door taller than your dad? Metres and centimetres can tell!
points: We measure short lengths, like a pencil, in centimetres (cm).
We measure longer lengths, like a room or a rope, in metres (m).
1 metre = 100 centimetres.
To change metres to centimetres, multiply by 100: 3 m = 300 cm.
1 m 30 cm means 100 cm + 30 cm = 130 cm.

example.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?

learn.reallife: A tailor measures you in centimetres. A cloth shop sells cloth by the metre.

quiz.q: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
quiz.explain: 1 metre is the same as 100 centimetres.
steps: The metre is the bigger unit; the centimetre is the smaller one.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metres with kilograms (1000) or with minutes (60)

quiz.q: Which unit is best to measure the length of a pencil?
quiz.explain: A pencil is short, so we use centimetres. Kilogram measures weight and litre measures liquid.
steps: A pencil is short, so use a small unit of length.
Centimetre is a small unit of length.
Kilogram is for weight and litre for liquid, so: Centimetre.
quiz.mistake: Picks a unit that does not measure length

quiz.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
Which rope is longer: one that is 1 m long or one that is 90 cm long?
quiz.explain: 1 m = 100 cm, and 100 cm is more than 90 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 90 is bigger than 1 without changing the units

quiz.q: A cloth piece is 400 cm long. How many metres is that?
quiz.explain: 100 cm make 1 m, so 400 cm make 400 ÷ 100 = 4 m.

quiz.q: Kabir's ruler is 30 cm long. How many such rulers placed end to end make exactly 3 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change 3 m into 300 cm

quiz.q: Riya is 1 m 30 cm tall. What is her height in centimetres?
quiz.mistake: Writes 1 and 30 side by side, or writes 1 m as 1000 cm

quiz.q: Which length is the longest?
quiz.explain: Change all to cm: 2 m = 200 cm, 199 cm, 250 cm, 1 m 90 cm = 190 cm. 250 cm is the longest.
quiz.mistake: Compares numbers without changing them to the same unit

teach.ask: Gappu measured a rope: 2 m. Kabir says it is 200 cm. Who is right?
teach.praise: Both are right! 1 m is 100 cm, so 2 m is 200 cm. Gappu is happy!
teach.nudge: How many centimetres are in one metre? Can two answers both be correct?

revise.summary: We measure short lengths like a pencil in centimetres and longer lengths like a room in metres. 1 metre = 100 centimetres.
focus: Choose cm or m for a length
Change m to cm and cm to m
Compare lengths after changing to the same unit
remember: 1 metre = 100 centimetres
m to cm: multiply by 100 (3 m = 300 cm)
traps: 1 m is not 1000 cm or 60 cm
Don't multiply or divide by 10 instead of 100
Don't compare numbers without changing them to the same unit

topics.title: Fractions of a metre and measuring small things

learn.hook: Half a metre, a quarter metre, three-quarters of a metre... in centimetres, they are 50, 25 and 75!
points: Half a metre = 50 cm. A quarter metre = 25 cm. Three-quarters of a metre = 75 cm.
Measure small objects with a scale: put one end at 0 and read the number at the other end.
After measuring, we can order things from shortest to longest.
About 1 cm long: a fingernail's width, a peanut, a small bead, a staple pin.

example.q: A ribbon is three-quarters of a metre long. How many cm is that?

learn.reallife: At a cloth shop, you can buy half a metre or a quarter metre of ribbon for a rakhi or a craft project.

quiz.q: How many centimetres are in a quarter metre?
Which is three-quarters of a metre?
Lengths: pencil 14 cm, eraser 4 cm, crayon 9 cm. Which list is shortest to longest?
steps: Lengths: eraser 4 cm, crayon 9 cm, pencil 14 cm.
Shortest to longest: eraser, crayon, pencil.

quiz.q: Which is about 1 cm long?
steps: 1 cm is very small, about the width of a fingertip.
A pen, a bag and a bat are much longer.
A peanut is about 1 cm long.

quiz.q: A scale shows one end of a leaf at 0 and the other end at 7. How long is the leaf?
quiz.explain: Starting at 0, the end mark gives the length: 7 cm.
steps: The leaf starts at the 0 mark.
When an object starts at 0, the end mark gives the length.
The end is at 7, so the leaf is 7 cm long.

quiz.q: Mira has half a metre of lace and needs 75 cm. How much more lace does she need?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change half a metre into cm

quiz.q: Two quarter-metre strips are joined. How long is the joined strip?
quiz.explain: 25 + 25 = 50 cm, which is half a metre.

quiz.q: Which is longest: 3/4 m, 70 cm, half a metre?
quiz.explain: 3/4 m = 75 cm, more than 70 cm and 50 cm.
steps: Change all to cm. 3/4 m = 3 × 25 = 75 cm.
Half a metre = 50 cm; the other is 70 cm.
75 cm is the biggest, so 3/4 m is longest.
quiz.mistake: Does not change fractions of a metre into cm

teach.ask: Gappu wants a quarter metre of ribbon but the shopkeeper asks 'how many centimetres?' Help Gappu.
teach.praise: A quarter metre is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 cm. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many cm are in a metre, and how do you find a quarter of it?

revise.summary: Half a metre is 50 cm, a quarter metre is 25 cm and three-quarters of a metre is 75 cm. Measure small objects with a scale by putting one end at 0.
focus: Change fractions of a metre into cm
Measure with a scale starting at 0
Order lengths from shortest to longest
remember: Put one end at 0 and read the number at the other end
About 1 cm: a fingernail's width, a peanut, a small bead, a staple pin
traps: Don't write 3 and 4 side by side for 3/4 m
Don't compare fractions of a metre with cm until you change them into cm
Don't add 1 for the starting mark

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Your hand and feet can help you guess lengths.
points: To estimate means to make a smart guess, close to the real answer.
Use body measures: a handspan is about 15 cm, a big step is about 50 cm for a child.
A door is about 2 m tall. A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. An eraser is about 4 cm long.
Check your guess by measuring. A good estimate is close to the real length.

example.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?

learn.reallife: Before buying a mat, you can step across the room to guess if it will fit.

games.title: Good estimate?
items: A classroom door is about 2 m tall.
That is a little taller than most grown-ups.
A pencil is about 2 m long.
A pencil is about 15 to 20 cm long.
An eraser is about 4 cm long.
It fits easily in your hand.
A school bus is about 50 cm long.
A bus is many metres long.
A cricket bat is closer to 1 m than to 1 cm.
A cricket bat is a bit less than 1 m long.
A grain of rice is about 1 m long.
It is only a few millimetres, much less than 1 cm.

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
quiz.explain: A door is a little taller than a grown-up, which is about 2 m.
steps: A door is a little taller than a grown-up.
A grown-up is a bit less than 2 m tall.
So about 2 m. (2 cm is too small; 20 m and 200 m are too big.)
quiz.mistake: Picks the right number with the wrong unit

quiz.q: What is the best estimate for the length of an eraser?
quiz.explain: An eraser fits in your palm, so it is only a few centimetres long.
steps: An eraser fits in your palm.
So it is only a few centimetres long.
About 4 cm is the best estimate.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture how big a metre is

quiz.q: Riya's handspan is about 15 cm. Her table is 6 handspans long. About how long is the table?
quiz.explain: 6 handspans of 15 cm each is 6 × 15 = 90 cm.
steps: One handspan ≈ 15 cm. The table is 6 handspans.

quiz.q: Arjun's step is about 50 cm long. About how many steps will he take to walk 5 m?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change metres to centimetres

quiz.q: Which of these is closest to 1 m long?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is a little less than 1 m long. The others are much smaller or much bigger.
steps: A matchbox and a rice grain are tiny; a school bus is many metres long.
A cricket bat is a little less than 1 m, so it is the closest.
quiz.mistake: Does not have a picture of 1 m in mind

quiz.q: Kabir guessed that his book was 40 cm long. He measured it and it was 32 cm. How far off was his guess?
quiz.explain: 40 - 32 = 8 cm. His guess was 8 cm too long.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which of these would you measure in metres?
quiz.explain: A cricket pitch is long, about 20 m. The others are small and are measured in cm or smaller.
steps: Metres are used for long things.
An ant, a coin and a pencil are small (cm or less).
A cricket pitch is about 20 m long, so measure it in metres.
Answer: Length of a cricket pitch
quiz.mistake: Thinks metres are used for small things

quiz.q: A cricket pitch is about 20 m long. Meena walks along it 3 times. About how far does she walk?
steps: One walk along the pitch ≈ 20 m. Meena walks 3 times.

teach.ask: Gappu has no ruler but wants to know how long the bench is. What can Gappu do?
teach.praise: Smart! Use handspans or steps to estimate, then check with a ruler later. Gappu tried it!
teach.nudge: What could Gappu use from Gappu's own body to guess the length?

revise.summary: To estimate means to make a smart guess close to the real answer. Use body measures and known lengths, then check by measuring.
focus: Choose the best estimate with the right unit
Estimate lengths using handspans and steps
Find how far off a guess was
remember: Handspan about 15 cm; a child's big step about 50 cm
Door about 2 m tall; cricket pitch about 20 m long; eraser about 4 cm long
traps: Don't pick the right number with the wrong unit
Multiply, don't add: 6 handspans of 15 cm is 90 cm
Don't divide metres by a step length in cm; change m to cm first

topics.title: Ramps, treasure maps and broken scales

learn.hook: Your scale is broken and starts at 3! Can you still measure? Yes, with one clever subtraction.
points: To find how far a toy car rolls, measure from where it starts to where it stops, in cm.
On a map where each step is 1 cm, add the cm of each part of a route to find its length.
Compare routes to find the longest and shortest.
With a broken scale, length = end mark − start mark. From 3 to 11 is 11 − 3 = 8 cm.

example.q: A pencil is placed on a broken scale from the 4 cm mark to the 13 cm mark. How long is it?

learn.reallife: If your scale's zero is worn off, you can still measure by starting at 1 cm and taking away 1 from the reading!

quiz.q: A broken scale starts at 2 cm. A crayon goes from 2 to 10. How long is the crayon?
steps: The crayon starts at 2 and ends at 10 on the broken scale.

quiz.q: A toy car starts at the 15 cm mark and stops at the 62 cm mark on a tape. How far did it roll?
steps: Start = 15 cm mark; stop = 62 cm mark.

quiz.q: Car A rolls 48 cm down a ramp. Car B rolls 39 cm. How much further did car A go?
steps: Car A = 48 cm; Car B = 39 cm.

quiz.q: On a treasure map each step is 1 cm. Route 1: 4 cm + 3 cm + 2 cm. Route 2: 5 cm + 5 cm. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: Route 1 = 9 cm, Route 2 = 10 cm. Route 1 is shorter.

quiz.q: How long is route 4 cm + 6 cm + 5 cm on the map?
A ribbon lies on a broken scale from 7 cm to 19 cm. How long is it?
steps: The ribbon goes from 7 cm to 19 cm.

quiz.q: Why can't you just read the end number on a broken scale?
options: The object does not start at 0
quiz.explain: The object starts at a mark that is not 0, so you must subtract the start.
steps: On a broken scale, the object does not start at 0.
The end number includes the part before the start.
So you must subtract the start mark from the end mark.
Answer: The object does not start at 0

quiz.q: A toy car rolls 25 cm from a low ramp and 40 cm from a high ramp. How much further from the high ramp?
steps: High ramp = 40 cm; low ramp = 25 cm.

teach.ask: Gappu's scale broke and now starts at 5. Gappu measured a stick from 5 to 17 and says 17 cm. Help Gappu.
teach.praise: 17 minus 5 is 12 cm! The stick did not start at 0.
teach.nudge: Where does the stick start, and what should you do with that number?

revise.summary: To find how far something rolls or how long it is, take the end mark minus the start mark. Add the cm of each part of a map route to find its length.
focus: Measure with a broken scale
Find distances rolled by toy cars
Add and compare route lengths on a map
remember: Length = end mark − start mark
From 3 to 11 is 11 − 3 = 8 cm
traps: Don't read only the end mark
Don't add the two marks
Compare total lengths, not the number of parts

learn.hook: A rope is 2 m long. How many 20 cm pieces can you cut from it? Let's find out!
points: On a number line, 1 m 50 cm sits halfway between 1 m and 2 m.
Mark metres on a number line, and centimetres between them: 100 cm, 150 cm, 200 cm.
To find how many pieces fit, change to the same unit and divide: 2 m = 200 cm, 200 ÷ 20 = 10.
Equal lengths can be written in different ways: 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm, and 4 m = 400 cm.

example.q: How many 25 cm pieces can be cut from a 2 m ribbon?

learn.reallife: Well depths, saree lengths and rope lengths are written in m and cm. Shopkeepers change them to cm to cut pieces.

quiz.q: How many 20 cm pieces can be cut from a 2 m rope?
On a number line marked 0 m, 1 m, 2 m, where is 1 m 50 cm?
quiz.explain: 1 m 50 cm is 50 cm more than 1 m and 50 cm less than 2 m.
steps: 1 m = 100 cm and 2 m = 200 cm; 150 is 50 more than 100 and 50 less than 200.
So it is halfway between 1 m and 2 m.
Answer: Halfway between 1 m and 2 m

quiz.q: Three wells are 305 cm, 3 m 50 cm and 3 m 5 cm deep. Which two are equally deep?
steps: Change all to cm: 305 cm; 3 m 50 cm = 350 cm; 3 m 5 cm = 300 + 5 = 305 cm.
So 305 cm and 3 m 5 cm are equally deep.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 450 cm?
A number line goes 100 cm, 120 cm, 140 cm, ? What is the next mark?
quiz.explain: It goes up by 20 cm each time: 140 + 20 = 160.
steps: 100 → 120 → 140: it goes up by 20 cm each time.

quiz.q: How many 50 cm pieces can be cut from a 3 m cloth?
A well is 6 m 8 cm deep. How many cm is that?
quiz.mistake: Writes 6 and 8 side by side as 68

quiz.q: Rita cuts 15 cm pieces from a 90 cm ribbon. How many pieces?

teach.ask: Gappu has a 2 m rope and wants 20 cm pieces for a craft. How can Gappu find how many pieces?
teach.praise: 2 m is 200 cm, and 200 ÷ 20 = 10 pieces. Craft time!
teach.nudge: What unit should both lengths be in, and then what do you do?

revise.summary: Metres and centimetres can be shown on a number line, and the same length can be written in different ways. To find how many pieces fit, change to the same unit and divide.
focus: Place m and cm on a number line
Change between m and cm, like 3 m 5 cm = 305 cm
Find how many pieces can be cut
remember: 1 m 50 cm is halfway between 1 m and 2 m
3 m 5 cm = 305 cm
traps: 3 m 5 cm is not 350 cm
Don't divide 2 by 20; change 2 m to 200 cm first
6 m 8 cm is 608 cm, not 68

learn.hook: Stand against the wall, put a book flat on your head and mark it. How tall are you?
points: Measure height from the floor to the top of the head, standing straight against a wall.
Record each child's height in a table, in cm or in m and cm.
The tallest child has the biggest height; the shortest has the smallest.
1 m = 100 cm. Children taller than 1 m have heights more than 100 cm.

example.q: Heights: Anu 128 cm, Bilal 1 m 35 cm, Chinku 98 cm. Who is the tallest? Who is shorter than 1 m?
example.answer: Bilal is tallest; Chinku is shorter than 1 m

learn.reallife: Doctors measure children's height at check-ups to see how much they have grown.

quiz.q: Heights: Rina 132 cm, Sonu 1 m 25 cm, Tia 1 m 40 cm. Who is the tallest?
steps: Change all to cm: Rina 132 cm; Sonu 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm; Tia 1 m 40 cm = 140 cm.

quiz.q: In that group, how much taller is Tia than Sonu?
steps: Tia = 1 m 40 cm = 140 cm; Sonu = 1 m 25 cm = 125 cm.

quiz.q: A class records: 95 cm, 104 cm, 99 cm, 112 cm, 101 cm. How many children are taller than 1 m?
steps: 1 m = 100 cm. Taller than 1 m means more than 100 cm.
95 and 99 are less; 104, 112 and 101 are more.
So 3 children are taller than 1 m.

quiz.q: How should you stand to measure your height correctly?
options: Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
quiz.explain: Standing straight with heels on the floor gives the true height.
steps: To measure the true height, nothing should add or take away height.
Tall shoes add height; bending your knees takes it away.
So stand straight against a wall with feet flat.
Answer: Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
quiz.mistake: Does not think about fair measuring

quiz.q: Asha is 1 m 18 cm tall. What is her height in cm?
Heights: 120 cm, 97 cm, 108 cm. Who is the shortest?
steps: The heights are 120 cm, 97 cm and 108 cm.
The shortest is the smallest number: 97.
So the one at 97 cm is the shortest.

quiz.q: Ravi was 110 cm tall last year. Now he is 1 m 17 cm. How much did he grow?
steps: Now: 1 m 17 cm = 100 + 17 = 117 cm. Last year: 110 cm.

quiz.q: Heights: 98 cm, 1 m 2 cm, 99 cm, 1 m 10 cm. How many are shorter than 1 m?
quiz.explain: 98 cm and 99 cm are shorter than 100 cm.
steps: Shorter than 100 cm: 98 cm and 99 cm.

teach.ask: Gappu's class wants to find the tallest child. Explain how to measure and compare heights.
teach.praise: Measure straight against the wall, write it in a table, and the biggest number is the tallest!
teach.nudge: How do you measure fairly, and how do you find the tallest?

revise.summary: Measure height from the floor to the top of the head, standing straight against a wall. Record heights in a table and compare: children taller than 1 m are more than 100 cm.
focus: Find the tallest and shortest from a table
Change heights in m and cm into cm
Count heights more or less than 1 m
remember: 1 m 18 cm = 118 cm
Stand straight against a wall with feet flat
traps: Don't compare only the cm part without the metres
99 cm is not taller than 1 m
1 m 18 cm is not 1018 cm

topics.title: Perimeter: the boundary around a shape

learn.hook: A farmer wants to put a fence around his field. How much fencing wire does he need?
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary around a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
If a garden's edge is lined with bricks, count the bricks along the boundary to find its length in bricks.
A rectangle 5 m long and 3 m wide has perimeter 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m.
You can estimate, then measure, the perimeter of real things like a book, a table or a lid.

example.q: A table top is 120 cm long and 60 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

learn.reallife: Lace stitched around a handkerchief, a fence around a field and a boundary wall around a school all show perimeter.

games.title: Perimeter facts
items: Perimeter is the length around the outside of a shape.
It is the total boundary length.
To find perimeter, multiply length by width.
A square with side 5 cm has perimeter 20 cm.
Lace around a handkerchief measures its perimeter.
The lace goes along the boundary.
It is a length, so cm or m.

quiz.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
A square garden has sides of 9 m. How much fencing goes around it?
steps: A square has 4 equal sides of 9 m.

quiz.q: A garden is lined with bricks: 10 bricks on each long side and 6 on each short side. How many bricks in all on the boundary? (No brick is shared at the corners.)
steps: Boundary = long side + short side + long side + short side.

quiz.q: What is perimeter?
options: The total length around a shape
quiz.explain: Perimeter is the length of the boundary.
steps: Perimeter is the boundary around a shape.
It is found by adding the lengths of all the sides.
So perimeter is the total length around a shape (not the space inside).
Answer: The total length around a shape

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. What is its perimeter?
steps: Perimeter of a triangle = sum of its 3 sides.

quiz.q: Gopal guessed his book's perimeter is 100 cm. He measured sides of 25 cm and 20 cm. What is the true perimeter?
quiz.explain: 25 + 20 + 25 + 20 = 90 cm. His guess was 10 cm too much.
steps: A book is a rectangle: sides 25, 20, 25, 20 cm.
= 90 cm. (His guess, 100 cm, was 10 cm too much.)

quiz.q: Lace is put around a square handkerchief of side 30 cm. How much lace is needed?
steps: A square handkerchief has 4 equal sides of 30 cm.

quiz.q: A rectangular field is 50 m long and 30 m wide. Mohan walks once around it. How far does he walk?

teach.ask: Gappu wants to put ribbon around a photo frame. How can Gappu find how much ribbon is needed?
teach.praise: Measure each side and add them all. That is the perimeter!
teach.nudge: Which sides do you measure, and what do you do with the numbers?

revise.summary: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary around a shape. To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
focus: Find the perimeter of rectangles, squares and triangles
Count bricks along a boundary
Solve fence and lace problems
remember: Perimeter = add the lengths of all the sides
Rectangle 5 m by 3 m: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m
Square of side 9 m: 4 × 9 = 36 m
traps: Don't add only two sides
Don't multiply the side by itself for a square's perimeter
Perimeter is not area

topics.title: Comparing boundaries: same perimeter, different shapes

learn.hook: A 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square look different. Yet their boundaries are exactly the same length!
points: On a dot grid, count the units along the boundary to compare shapes.
Different shapes can have the same perimeter: a 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square both have perimeter 12 units.
To find the shape with the smallest boundary, find each perimeter and compare.
To draw shapes with perimeter 20 cm, the length and width must add to 10: 5 by 5, 6 by 4, 7 by 3, 8 by 2, 9 by 1.

example.q: Draw two different rectangles with perimeter 20 cm.
steps: Length + width must be half of 20, which is 10.
example.answer: 6 cm by 4 cm, and 8 cm by 2 cm

learn.reallife: Two gardens can need the same length of fence even if one is long and thin and the other is square.

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a 4 by 2 rectangle on a dot grid?
steps: A 4 by 2 rectangle has sides 4, 2, 4, 2 units.

quiz.q: Which has the same perimeter as a 3 by 3 square?
steps: Only the 4 by 2 rectangle has perimeter 12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only identical shapes have the same perimeter

quiz.q: Garden A: 6 m by 2 m. Garden B: 4 m by 4 m. Garden C: 5 m by 2 m. Which has the smallest boundary?
quiz.explain: A: 16 m. B: 16 m. C: 14 m. C is smallest.

quiz.q: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and length 7 cm. What is its width?
Which rectangle does NOT have a perimeter of 20 cm?
steps: Perimeter of a rectangle = length + breadth + length + breadth.

quiz.q: Two shapes on a dot grid: an L-shape with perimeter 14 units and a rectangle 5 by 2. Which has the longer boundary?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a different shape must have a different perimeter

quiz.q: A square has perimeter 20 cm. How long is each side?
How many different rectangles with whole-cm sides have perimeter 12 cm? (Count 2 by 4 and 4 by 2 as the same.)
quiz.explain: Length + width = 6: 5 by 1, 4 by 2, 3 by 3. That is 3.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a long thin rectangle always has a bigger boundary than a square. Show Gappu an example.
teach.praise: A 3 by 3 square and a 4 by 2 rectangle both have 12! Shapes can look different and still have the same boundary.
teach.nudge: Can you find a square and a rectangle with the same perimeter?

revise.summary: Different shapes can have the same perimeter, like a 4 by 2 rectangle and a 3 by 3 square. For a rectangle with perimeter 20 cm, the length and width must add to 10.
focus: Find and compare perimeters on a dot grid
Find a missing side from the perimeter
Draw different rectangles with the same perimeter
remember: 4 by 2 rectangle and 3 by 3 square: both 12 units
Perimeter 20 cm: length + width = 10 (5 by 5, 6 by 4, 7 by 3, 8 by 2, 9 by 1)
Square with perimeter 20 cm: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm
traps: Don't multiply length × width for perimeter
Don't think different shapes must have different perimeters
Don't take the length from 20: length + width = 10, so a 7 cm length gives a 3 cm width
